title: Stability of regular linear threshold functions
statement:
There is a real constant $C\geq0$ such that for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every real-valued function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, every coefficient family $(a_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,n}$, and every $\varepsilon,\rho\in\mathbb R$, the following holds. If $f(x)$ is the threshold sign, with zero assigned sign $1$, of $\sum_i a_i\sigma(x_i)$ for every $x$, this sum is nonzero for every $x$, $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, $|a_i|\leq\varepsilon$ for every $i$, and $|\rho|<1$, then
\[\left|\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)-\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin\rho\right|\leq\frac{C\sqrt{\varepsilon}}{1-\rho},\]
where $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)$ is the inner product of $f$ with its noise operator at parameter $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube
The function equals the threshold sign of the homogeneous linear form at every input
The homogeneous linear form is nonzero at every input
The sum of squared coefficients equals $1$
replaced: There exists a universal real constant $C\ge0$ with the following property. For every $n\ge0$, real coefficients $a_i$, and real $\varepsilon,\rho$ with $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$, $|\rho|<1$, and $\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i}\ne0$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $f(x)$ equal $1$ when $\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i}\ge0$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then $|\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)-(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho|\le C\sqrt{\max(\varepsilon,0)}/(1-\rho)$. For a real function $h$ on a uniform bit cube, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(h)=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}\widehat h(S)^2$.
